goal: Expose return-lint.mjs's verdict-block extraction as a named export so B1's gates.mjs can read a reviewer's parsed {verdict, findings} without re-parsing markdown. Purely additive and behavior-preserving: extract the body of verdictBlockViolations into a new exported extractVerdictBlock(body) that returns either the parsed verdict object or the exact violation it already returns today, and reimplement verdictBlockViolations on top of it. No behavior change, no new failure mode, no schema_version event.
constraints: conventions.md 'a fenced ## Findings example satisfied required_sections — an accept-a-fake hole' (backend-notes.md 2026-08-02): the fence-aware realHeadings/extractSection/extractFencedBlocks trio must be reused verbatim, never widened, never duplicated.
conventions.md 2026-08-08 'a frozen exported enum's drift guard needs Object.isFrozen alongside deepEqual' — if you freeze anything new, pin both.
conventions.md 2026-08-01 'every functional commit bumps plugin.json' — NOT in this spec; be-28-03 owns the single bump for this PR.
backend-notes.md 2026-08-01 'throw on contract-author error, return violations on data error' — extractVerdictBlock returns a discriminated result, never throws on worker data.

Behavior-preserving refactor only: verdictBlockViolations' externally observable output must be byte-identical for every input, including the guard clauses (verdict_block false, kind !== 'markdown', non-string body) which stay in verdictBlockViolations and are NOT moved into extractVerdictBlock.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/cmux/return-lint.mjs exports extractVerdictBlock(body) with signature: returns {ok: true, verdict, findings} on success, or {ok: false, keyword, message} where keyword is one of the existing exported constants VERDICT_SECTION_MISSING / VERDICT_BLOCK_MISSING / VERDICT_BLOCK_MULTIPLE / VERDICT_BLOCK_UNPARSEABLE / VERDICT_BLOCK_INVALID and message is the corresponding existing *_MESSAGE constant (with the same err.message / schema-detail suffixes appended as today).

verdictBlockViolations is reimplemented as: its three existing guard clauses, then `const res = extractVerdictBlock(envelope.body); return res.ok ? [] : [{ keyword: res.keyword, message: res.message }]`. No other change to the function.

Every pre-existing test in test/return-lint.test.mjs passes unmodified — proof the refactor is behavior-preserving. If any pre-existing test needed editing, that is a behavior change and the coder must return `blocked` rather than edit it.

New tests in test/return-lint.test.mjs, positives first: (1) a body with a real '## Verdict' section containing one ```json block returns {ok:true} with the exact verdict string and findings array; (2) a body containing BOTH an illustrative fenced example that itself contains a '## Verdict' heading AND the real Verdict section returns the REAL block's values — the pin that the fence-aware realHeadings path is actually being used; (3) each of the five failure keywords is produced by its own single-mutation negative, asserted with deepEqual on the full {ok:false, keyword, message} object (exactly one result, right reason — backend-notes.md 2026-08-01 Violation-shape rule); (4) all three VERDICT_ENUM values ('pass','changes-needed','inconclusive') round-trip through {ok:true}; (5) a Verdict section with one ```json block plus one untagged illustrative block returns the json-tagged one (the SF2 disambiguation path).
Degenerate assertion: a stub extractVerdictBlock that always returns {ok:true, verdict:'pass', findings:[]} must fail at least three of the new tests — state in a comment which ones.

Review depth: code-reviewer-deep is REQUIRED (scripts/cmux/*.mjs is the contract-freeze surface, config.md review_defaults line 46) and this file participates in the adversarial 3-reviewer panel + test-engineer mutation pass already decided for issue #28 by the qa-lead consult. The mutation pass runs first and alone on the frozen tree.
`node --test test/return-lint.test.mjs` green; no new test takes measurable wall time (pure string functions, no spawn, no git, no fs).
out_of_scope: Any change to lintReturn, writeBlockedReturn, buildBlockedMarkdownBody, destinationHoldsFreshNonBlockedReturn, main, or the CLI surface.
Widening or altering the fence-tracking semantics of realHeadings / extractSection / extractFencedBlocks.
Any change to VERDICT_SCHEMA, VERDICT_ENUM, SEVERITY_ENUM, or any *_MESSAGE constant text.
Any file under scripts/chain/ — that is be-28-02 and be-28-03.
Bumping .claude-plugin/plugin.json — be-28-03 owns the single bump for this PR.
interface_contract: extractVerdictBlock(body: string) -> { ok: true, verdict: 'pass'|'changes-needed'|'inconclusive', findings: object[] } | { ok: false, keyword: string, message: string }. Backend (this task) owns this shape; be-28-03's gates.mjs verdict_consistent check consumes it and must not redefine or re-derive it. `keyword` is always one of the five exported VERDICT_* constants from scripts/cmux/return-lint.mjs.
